about: #82 (ADR 0020): the probe of the words, fixed before any request. Three arms on the same packets, interleaved request by request; the lines, the rule choosing among the arms, the outside calls, the stand-in requirement and each check's right value are here first. Version 1.

arms.0: old: src/plan/forms.ts checkBeforeAction.observationQuestions as committed (assume the case, because the check it asks for does not pass)
arms.1: case only: the function's question of arm 2 without any check clause (no check is read); 'unless the case itself decides it otherwise' included; nothing about names
arms.2: two-step: for each check sent (depth 1), the check-value question on the check's own body (its depth-2 bodies as related); then the function's question assuming each value read. A check read as cannot_determine, or under 0.6, holds: the function's question is not sent for that arm and run, and the hold is recorded

wording.function: `code` is the body of `{F}`. The entries under `evidence.related` are the bodies of functions `{F}` calls, given so that what those calls do can be read. Assume exactly this and nothing else: `{F}` is called in the case `requirement.text` describes, the one in which it says the call `{X}` must not be made{VALUES}; every other operation the function reaches succeeds, unless the case itself decides it otherwise. Under that condition: does `{F}` go on to make the call `{X}`?
wording.check: `code` is the body of `{CNAME}`, which `{F}` calls as `{C}`. The entries under `evidence.related` are the bodies of functions `{CNAME}` calls, given so that what those calls do can be read. Take the case `requirement.text` describes, the one in which it says the call `{X}`, made in `{F}`, must not be made. In that case, what does `{C}` return?

check_criteria.cannot_determine: The code shown does not settle which.

wording.function_criteria: REACH_CRITERIA as src has them (read from the old question at run time, so the three answers are the same words in every arm)

order: for each target, for each run 1..3: arm 0, arm 1, arm 2 (its check questions, then its function question); then the outside calls the same way

lines.check_values: arm 2: for every check with a value in `values`, the check-value answer is that value at or above 0.6 in at least 2 of 3 runs (helper: returns_false_or_err; hidden: returns_true_or_ok; shipped/rewrite/defect checks as listed). An answer that is the same for every check fails hidden or helper.
lines.hidden: H (3 targets): reaches_it at or above 0.6 in at least 2 of 3 runs of each target, and does_not_reach at or above 0.6 in 0 of 9
lines.defect: D (3 targets): reaches_it at or above 0.6 in at least 2 of 3 runs of each target
lines.settled: S (9 targets: shipped, rewrite, helper): reaches_it at or above 0.6 in 0 of 27, and does_not_reach at or above 0.6 in at least 2 of 3 runs of each target
lines.outside: of the outside runs arm 0 read as does_not_reach at or above 0.6 (at least 10 runs, or the probe is redesigned and nothing is adopted), the adopted arm reads none as reaches_it at or above 0.6, and at most 30% as cannot_determine, under the bar, or held
not_gated: arm 0 on the same packets, as the control
the net: a check whose body reads none of its parameters, scored on the 15 targets
arm 1's check values are not a thing; arm 1 has no check question

adoption: arm 2 if it meets every line above; else arm 1 if it meets hidden, defect, settled and outside; else nothing is wired and the numbers go to the owner. No exception for grovedb-500: a shipped or rewrite version read as reaches_it fails the arm whatever the sentence's shape.
